It offers create, edit and delete methods for both. `writeFiles()` flushes every changed schema to disk. `rollback()` restores the previous files. If a write fails, the builder rolls back and the service throws `Invalid schema edition`. When a component changes category, its uid changes too. `writeFiles()` then calls `renameComponentRows()`, which rewrites the stored uid in one transaction: `component_type` in the `*_cmps` join tables and the type column of the polymorphic tables, for example `related_type` in `files_related_mph` for media. This runs before the reload, while `strapi.db.metadata` still locates those tables. If the rewrite fails, the builder rolls back the files. `updateSchema` and the kind change of `editContentType` call `writeFiles({ renameComponentRows: false })` and then `renameComponentRows({ beforeCommit })`, which writes `groups.json` inside the row transaction, after the rewrite and before the commit. A failed folder commit therefore rolls the rows back as well, and the caller restores the files. The `beforeCommit` callback must not query the database: the transaction holds the only connection of a SQLite pool. If the database `COMMIT` itself fails after `groups.json` is written, `groups.json` keeps the new folder layout; this is harmless, because unknown uids are dropped when the file is read. Content-history versions keep the old uid in their JSON `data`, so a version saved before the move cannot be restored after it. The rewrite runs only against the database of the instance that saved the change: other databases that receive the new schema files (staging, production) lose the entries of the moved component at their next boot that syncs a schema change, unless the rename is replayed there.

The admin panel does not save one attribute at a time. It sends the whole change set to `POST /content-type-builder/update-schema`. Each content type, component and attribute in the payload has an `action` (`create`, `update` or `delete`). The `schema` service applies the payload to the builder, writes the files, generates or clears API folders, and commits the folder groups last. On error, `rollbackSchemaMutation` restores the touched files. Code: [`services/schema.ts`](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/packages/core/content-type-builder/server/src/services/schema.ts).

-After the files are written, CTB emits `content-type.create|update|delete` and `component.create|update|delete` on `strapi.eventHub`, one event per changed schema. It awaits each event before the controller triggers the reload, for at most 2.5 seconds: past that, `emitSchemaEvent` logs a warning with `strapi.log.warn`, leaves the listeners running and moves on, so a listener that never settles cannot hang the save. If a listener throws, `emitSchemaEvent` logs the error with `strapi.log.error` and the request still succeeds, because the schema change is already on disk. Code: [`utils/events.ts`](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/develop/packages/core/content-type-builder/server/src/utils/events.ts).
